value.name: Miles lies passed out in guest room
value.description: Miles is found asleep or passed out in a filthy guest room surrounded by empty wine bottles.
evidence: A guest room. Dark, dirty and filled with empty bottles of expensive French wine.
The figure on the bed stirs, rolls over, moans, clamps a pillow over his head.

value.name: Kenneth summons Miles to phone
value.description: Kenneth enters and tells Miles that a call is for him.
evidence: Kenneth enters the background, knotting a bathrobe. He turns on the light in the room.

value.name: Miles answers urgent phone call
value.description: Miles takes the phone and reacts with shock to the news he is hearing.
evidence: Miles blearily takes the offered phone.
MILES Hello. Yes -- what?! Yes -- I see --
After another listening beat he drops the phone away.

value.name: Miles learns Rex has died
value.description: Miles identifies the caller as Marvin Untermeyer and learns that Rex Rexroth has died of a massive coronary.
evidence: MILES He was Rex Rexroth's personal attorney.
MILES Rex just had a massive coronary. In the middle of a business meeting. He's dead.

value.name: Kenneth responds to Rex's death
value.description: Kenneth expresses mild sympathy but seems more puzzled than upset by the news.
evidence: KENNETH I'm sorry to hear that. But you weren't close, were you?

value.name: Miles realizes Marilyn inherits everything
value.description: Miles explains that Rex never updated his will, so Marilyn inherits the estate and remains married to him without a prenup.
evidence: MILES Marvin says that Rex's will is four years old. He never redrafted it.
MILES She's rich. We're still married. We have no pre-nup.

value.name: Kenneth asks if inheritance is good
value.description: Kenneth, still processing the news, asks whether Marilyn's inheritance is actually beneficial.
